dedupe_keys.name: recycling behaviour of chinese households netlogo model of a container and reward recycling experiment in a village near beijing

description: This NetLogo model represents a village on the outskirts of Beijing where an experiment used collectors, containers and rewards to encourage residents to recycle their valuable waste. It was published in the CoMSES library by Igor Nikolic with B. Dijkhuizen, M. van den Hoven and M. Minderhoud (version 1.1.0, 2018). The village has three areas: the university area, an area mostly of local residents, and an area of independent housing, with six containers placed where people could drop their waste. Household behaviour is tested with three different social theories, which lets the model compare explanations of how residents respond to the scheme. The code is available as a free download from CoMSES under a CC-BY-NC-4.0 licence (non-commercial). Caveats: it represents a single experiment, and the page does not report how well each theory matched the observed data. Coverage is one village in China. Simulation uses: testing the placement of recycling points and incentive schemes in waste collection planning. Related records: the residents' waste sorting model (model-comses-residents-waste-sorting-planned-behaviour) applies another behavioural theory to source separation.
